request.prompt: Create exactly one isolated full-body image of male Shepard wearing the complete Collector Armor from Mass Effect 2, matching the supplied original game-model reference views. Reference 1 is the controlling THREE-QUARTER pose and camera: neutral standing stance, both arms slightly away from the torso with relaxed visible gloved fingers, both boots planted and completely visible, helmet facing slightly toward image left. Reference 2 is the frontal corroboration of the exact same masculine armor, plate boundaries, straps, mesh undersuit, hands and boots. Reference 3 is the rear view of that same native model for hidden-part consistency only; do not create a rear-view figure or collage. Preserve the exact masculine proportions, organic gray-brown/lilac chitin plate shapes, muted red fibrous underlayers between plates, black woven undersuit and gloves, pale mechanical clasps on the chest and upper arms, paired buckled inner-thigh straps, dark knee hardware, long gray-black shin guards and the thick segmented boots. Reproduce the native in-game helmet shown in these references: layered pointed organic forehead plates, two small golden eye lenses, black center mask, thin horizontal protective lower-face bars, and the same collar. Do not substitute the separate promotional helmet, female version, Collector enemy anatomy, N7 armor, a different game or new accessories. Do not invent texture markings, wings, weapons, capes, spikes, exposed skin, extra plates or new clasps. Keep the restrained native texture detail and muted base colors; do not invent a glossy upgraded material or photorealistic surface. Preserve the exact reference A-pose rather than creating an unsupported combat stance. Entire helmet, hands, all fingertips and both complete boot soles inside the frame with at least 10 percent clear margins on all sides. Remove the gray inspection background, any floor and cast shadow. Real transparent alpha background; no scene, pedestal, halo, text, labels, border or sheet. One complete armored subject in one three-quarter view. These model inspection images establish geometry and diffuse texture; the output is a static prototype reference, not an engine material or animation.
